subsystems.name: Fiber feed and scrambling
subsystems.role: Brings starlight from the telescope focus to the spectrograph while smoothing spatial and angular variations.

subsystems.name: Echelle spectrograph optics
subsystems.role: Disperses the light into thousands of narrow spectral lines across many orders.

subsystems.name: Calibration unit
subsystems.role: Provides a reference spectrum simultaneously or before/after the stellar exposure to track instrumental drift.

subsystems.name: Vacuum and thermal enclosure
subsystems.role: Keeps the spectrograph at constant temperature and pressure so the optics do not drift.

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: Records the dispersed spectrum with high stability and low noise.

subsystems.name: Data reduction pipeline
subsystems.role: Converts raw frames into a wavelength-calibrated spectrum and a precise Doppler shift.

buildSteps.title: Define science requirements
buildSteps.detail: Set the target precision (e.g., 1 m/s), wavelength range, and resolution needed to measure stellar reflex motion.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical layout
buildSteps.detail: Choose echelle grating, cross-disperser, camera optics, and fiber feed to balance resolution, throughput, and stability.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and mount optics
buildSteps.detail: Machine a rigid optical bench from low-expansion material, polish and coat optics, and mount them with minimal play.

buildSteps.title: Build the vacuum and thermal enclosure
buildSteps.detail: Seal the spectrograph in a vacuum vessel and add active thermal control to hold temperature to a few thousandths of a degree.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the calibration system
buildSteps.detail: Install thorium-argon lamps and, where available, a laser frequency comb, with fiber routing to inject reference light.

buildSteps.title: Align and test in the laboratory
buildSteps.detail: Measure resolution, instrument profile, and short-term stability; iterate until the spectrograph meets specifications.

buildSteps.title: Install at the telescope
buildSteps.detail: Couple the fiber feed to the telescope, commission the instrument, and verify that it reaches the required precision on bright stars.

buildSteps.title: Operate with nightly calibration
buildSteps.detail: Take calibration frames each night, monitor long-term drift, and run the data pipeline to produce radial velocities and activity diagnostics.

prerequisites.why: They spread starlight into many lines, which is what makes tiny Doppler shifts measurable.
They provide an ideal wavelength ruler, but only some instruments have one; most still rely on thorium-argon lamps.
Without it, the spectrograph itself would drift more than the stellar signal being measured.
They collect enough photons from faint stars to reach high precision in reasonable exposure times.
Starspots and pulsations can mimic a planet, so they must be identified and corrected.

pathway.milestone: 1 m/s precision on bright stars with instruments like HARPS and ESPRESSO
pathway.unlocks: Masses for many transiting planets, especially Neptune-mass and larger.

pathway.milestone: 10 cm/s precision using laser frequency combs and extreme stabilization
pathway.unlocks: Detection of Earth-mass planets around Sun-like stars.

pathway.milestone: Dedicated extreme-precision spectrographs on large and future extremely large telescopes
pathway.unlocks: Masses for small planets found by transit surveys, and better target selection for biosignature searches.

pathway.milestone: Routine combination of radial velocity with astrometry and direct imaging
pathway.unlocks: Full orbital and atmospheric characterization of habitable-zone planets.
